mentions.title: WARNING about King Main Thrust Bearings
mentions.snippet: Explicit buyer-warning thread claiming King main thrust bearings from the 2024 and 2025 production runs are out of spec on free spread, with the poster stating King tech support confirmed the bearings should not be used. Spans more than one production year.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: King Main Bearings Defective
mentions.snippet: Reports that King thrust bearings are over 1mm too narrow to fit BMW S85 and S65 blocks, framed as a defect affecting the part as supplied rather than an install error.
mentions.replyNote: Still 307-redirects to the tollbit.m5board.com mirror instead of returning thread content, same as the previous check.

mentions.title: King Bearing - lack of professional help for quality control problem
mentions.snippet: Customer received a sealed King XP package with wrong shell quantities and says King declined to send a replacement half shell, directing him back to the supplier. Complaint is about service handling as much as the packing error.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: Just call it what it is---King Bearings are no longer an option....
mentions.snippet: Buyer-warning framing in the title, driven by long-running back-order and availability problems on 6-bolt applications since COVID with repeatedly pushed production dates.

mentions.title: King Bearing Failures?
mentions.snippet: Builder reports King main and rod bearings destroyed during break-in on a high-compression engine, requiring the crank to be turned; other posters in the thread attribute it to factors other than bearing quality.
mentions.replyNote: Still 307-redirects to the tollbit.460ford.com mirror instead of returning thread content, same as the previous check.

mentions.title: No more King XP bearings
mentions.snippet: Thread critical of King XP precision and sizing consistency; King has already posted an official response here.
mentions.replyNote: A new member account identifying as King Bearings posted an official response on 2026-08-04 addressing the precision concerns; thread remains open.
